material.advice: Watch out for the long sentence in chunk 4 and the slightly awkward phrasing in chunk 12 ('for ours to establish'). Break chunk 4 into two breaths: 'So it is getting more popular...' and 'and people believe...'. Use the keyword 'balance' in chunks 13-14 as a memory anchor to link the conclusion.

chunks.text: What you're doing right now is one clear example of brain rot.
It means that your brain is not functioning.
You're purely looking at things that we're not actually thinking.
So it is getting more popular among social media and people believe this action itself is really bad for your brain.
What I'm trying to say here is there's always a way to get rid of it.
chunks.hint: always a way to get rid

chunks.text: There's always a way to stop your brain from doing that.
So the way you're going to do that is take actions.
Make sure that every day that you understand you can practice your brain.
There are many things that you can prevent from brain rot.
On the other hand, social media is just fundamentally changing the way we were saving information.
It's important for ours to establish the awareness that too much time on social media probably not a good thing.
chunks.hint: awareness: too much time not good

chunks.text: As long as you understand that, I think there's a way to get a balance.
Balance is the key for us to best exercise our brain and become a better person.
